fixture_name: Cloverleaf-to-urban interchange conversion — INT preliminary design (Wikimedia PD geometry)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: A shortened collector-distributor weave carrying a recorded 1,100 pcu/h design-year peak flow is a classic, well-recognised sideswipe/rear-end exposure mechanism, and auditing it at preliminary design before geometry is fixed is squarely substantive for this scheme.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim rests on the recorded weave geometry/volume inputs plus a verbatim EV-IN-015 quote ('suitable for the function of the two roads, the traffic volume... Is there proper lane balance, and through lane continuity?') that directly supports the junction-suitability check demanded at preliminary design, exceeding the registry-citation cap.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly filed as a safety_concern with no compliance conflation, stage-appropriate to int:preliminary-design, and the PIARC-derived baseline is respected even though HSM/IHSDM are invoked only as supplementary analytical methods rather than normative requirements.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and staged: apply named Appendix 1 prompts to the identified weave, quantify via HSM Part C interchange models or IHSDM, and give conditional remedies (lengthen the CD section or ramp metering), making it actionable and viable at this design stage.
justifications.vru_coverage: Not applicable since the scenario records shared-use paths grade-separated from the motorised weave, but VRU exclusion is explicitly stated and reasoned, earning the acknowledgement score.

justifications.substance: Uncontrolled free-flow ramp-terminal crossings of retained shared-use paths at a preliminary-design interchange is a classic, substantive VRU safety issue directly tied to the recorded scheme objective of improved pedestrian/cycle continuity.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal normative claim is backed by verbatim quotes (EV-IN-016 junction-provision prompt; EV-IN-005 all-road-users/thematic-audit text), while scheme objectives and layout retention are flagged as recorded input facts; no invented content detected.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern for the INT preliminary-design stage, citing PIARC prompts as audit-checklist support rather than converting them into compliance findings; no conflation of compliance questions with safety concerns.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: apply thematic VRU audits plus Walkability Checklist/CQSI tools and deliver controlled or grade-separated (signalised) crossings at each shared-use path/ramp terminal interface, including naming the northern loop-ramp crossing; viable at preliminary design.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are the explicit focus, with their exposure at uncontrolled ramp-terminal crossings analysed as the core of the finding.
